name: California
summary: California IOU territory (SCE, PG&E, SDG&E) still offers some of the highest C&I demand charges in the US: an all-hours facilities/max-demand charge plus time-related demand charges in a 5-hour 4-9pm peak window. That makes bill-management (demand-charge reduction plus TOU arbitrage) the core value stream. The 4-9pm window is energy-limited for 2-hour products: a 200 kW/418 kWh unit can hold only about 84 kW flat across the full 5-hour window. The upfront-incentive landscape changed sharply. All ratepayer-funded SGIP budgets, including Large-Scale Storage, Non-Residential Storage Equity and Equity Resiliency, closed to new applications on 2025-12-31 (D.25-12-003; PU Code 379.6 sunset 2026-01-01). The remaining GGRF/AB 209 SGIP money is for low-income residential customers only. On the CEC side, the 2026 DSGS (Fifth Edition, adopted 2026-04-27) suspended Option 1, capped Option 2 at $1M, and limited Option 3 storage-VPP participation to aggregations that were active in October 2025. Absent new 2027 funding, the realistic stackable revenues for a new developer are therefore bill savings, ELRP ($2/kWh, pilot extended through 2027), CBP/CAISO PDR via an aggregator, and the federal ITC. Key site risks are the 2022/2025 CFC Section 1207 limits on indoor ESS (50 kWh per unit, 600 kWh Li-ion per fire area without approval), long LAFD/LACoFD/SFFD plan checks, Rule 21 non-export review, and secondary networks in downtown SF/Oakland/San Diego. Municipal utilities (LADWP, SMUD and others) are out of scope: they have their own tariffs, and the IOU programs and Rule 21 do not apply there.

utilities.name: Southern California Edison
utilities.default_supply_notes: Bundled customers pay SCE generation embedded in TOU energy and time-related demand charges. Many C&I sites are served by a CCA for generation, e.g. Clean Power Alliance, Orange County Power Authority, Desert Community Energy, San Jacinto Power, Rancho Mirage Energy Authority, 3CE, Santa Barbara Clean Energy, Lancaster, Pomona/PRIME. CCA customers keep SCE delivery charges, including the Facilities-Related Demand (FRD) charge, and pay a PCIA/CRS. Generation TOU and generation demand components are replaced by the CCA's rate, which usually mirrors SCE TOU periods. Direct Access is capped statewide, so it is not generally available to new customers.
utilities.network_grid_notes: SCE has limited secondary network service compared with PG&E or SDG&E. Some dense downtown or commercial cores may be served by network or spot-network systems. Confirm with SCE Grid Interconnection before sizing, because network PCCs fail standard Rule 21 Fast Track screens and require supplemental study, usually with strict non-export and minimum-import requirements. Not verified for specific cities.

interconnection.non_export_path: Rule 21 Screen I lets non-exporting facilities qualify by one of several options: (1) reverse-power protection, (2) minimum-power (minimum import) protection, (3) a relative-size limit versus the customer's minimum load, or (4) certified non-export equipment, i.e. a UL 1741-certified inverter with a Power Control System evaluated under UL 1741 CRD/PCS that limits export to near zero. The exact relay settings and percentage thresholds were not re-verified this session; confirm against the current Rule 21 Section G. Battery charging from the grid is load and is handled under Rule 15/16 and service-capacity rules, not Rule 21.
interconnection.storage_specific_notes: Smart-inverter (UL 1741 SA/SB, IEEE 1547) requirements apply to Rule 21 inverters. Non-export storage-only projects are usually the fastest path. Paired PV under the Net Billing Tariff (NBT) adds NEM/NBT-specific rules. Keep battery charging plus existing load within service and transformer capacity to avoid Rule 15/16 upgrade cost.

site_constraints.title: Rule 21 Screen I - non-exporting storage options
site_constraints.rule: BTM storage that will not export can pass Fast Track Screen I by one of several options: reverse-power protection, minimum-power (minimum import) protection, a relative-size limit versus minimum load, or certified non-export equipment (UL 1741-certified inverter with a UL 1741 CRD Power Control System limiting export). Passing allows an Interconnection Agreement without a detailed study.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Non-export lets battery kW exceed minimum site load only if the PCS caps discharge to follow load. Discharge kW is effectively limited to coincident site load in each interval, which caps the usable kW of 200 kW units at low-load sites. Relative-size and minimum-import options can further cap kW.

site_constraints.title: CFC Section 1207 applicability threshold for lithium-ion ESS
site_constraints.rule: Under the 2022 California Fire Code (based on the 2021 IFC), Section 1207 applies to stationary ESS above the threshold quantity in Table 1207.1.1, which is 20 kWh for lithium-ion. ESS must be listed to UL 9540, and AHJ permits and plan review are required.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: All four products exceed 20 kWh, so every project needs a fire permit under Section 1207.

site_constraints.title: Indoor ESS: 50 kWh per unit and 600 kWh lithium-ion per fire area
site_constraints.rule: Indoor ESS units are limited to 50 kWh each, with 3 ft spacing between units and from walls. The aggregate lithium-ion quantity within a room or fire area is limited to 600 kWh. Larger units or quantities need approval based on UL 9540A large-scale fire testing and a hazard mitigation analysis. These limits come from the 2021 IFC/2022 CFC Section 1207.5 as recalled and were not re-opened this session.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: The 150, 200, 418 and 600 kWh cabinets each exceed 50 kWh per unit, so indoor installs need UL 9540A-based approval. One 600 kWh unit consumes the entire per-fire-area allowance. Favor outdoor, pad-mounted installs.

site_constraints.title: Outdoor ESS separation (10 ft, reducible with UL 9540A)
site_constraints.rule: Outdoor ESS must be separated at least 10 ft from lot lines, public ways, buildings, stored combustibles and other exposures. The distance may be reduced (to about 3 ft) where UL 9540A large-scale fire test data and AHJ approval support it. Walk-in units are treated as rooms. Values are recalled from 2021 IFC 1207.8 and not re-opened.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Parking-lot and rear-of-building pads must satisfy setbacks. Tight urban retail sites may fit only one or two cabinets.

site_constraints.title: Title 24 Part 6 (2022, continued in 2025) - PV and battery requirements for new nonresidential buildings
site_constraints.rule: The 2022 Energy Code (effective 2023-01-01) requires solar PV, and battery storage where PV is required, for specified new nonresidential occupancies (e.g., offices, retail, grocery, schools, warehouses, hotels). Battery kWh and kW are sized by code formulas relative to PV size. The 2025 Energy Code (effective 2026-01-01) continues this. Formula factors and exceptions were not verified.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: New-construction sites may already have code-required storage, which reduces incremental retrofit value. Code-minimum batteries can be an upsell opportunity.

site_constraints.title: California Electrical Code - Article 706 ESS and 705.13 Power Control Systems
site_constraints.rule: ESS installations follow CEC (California Electrical Code) Article 706 and Article 705 interconnection rules. site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Switchgear busbar ratings and available breaker space often cap battery inverter kW at retail sites. A PCS can unlock headroom.

panel_notes.topic: FRD vs TRD and the 5-hour window
panel_notes.note: On TOU-GS-2/3 and TOU-8 Option D, the Facilities-Related Demand charge is set by the single highest 15-minute interval in any hour of the month. One morning HVAC spike can wipe out the savings, so dispatch must guard FRD all day, not just 4-9pm. The 4-9pm summer on-peak window is 5 hours, so a 200 kW/418 kWh unit can hold only about 84 kW flat across it (418/5).

panel_notes.topic: Option D vs E and CPP default
panel_notes.note: Re-run the Option D versus Option E comparison after commissioning. Storage nearly always favors D, but rate switches are limited (typically once per 12 months). Larger accounts default onto CPP, so CPP event days (4-9pm) need full state of charge at 4pm or the event adder erodes the month's savings.

On B-19/B-20, Option S converts most peak-period demand charges to daily charges. A missed dispatch costs one day rather than the month. That suits fleet operations and lower-confidence load forecasts. Confirm eligibility (storage size relative to peak) and whether the enrollment cap has room before modeling it.

Downtown San Francisco and Oakland network-served sites will not get through Fast Track. Expect supplemental review, strict minimum-import settings and a small allowable capacity. PG&E Rule 21 and Rule 15/16 queues are slow, so start interconnection and service-capacity requests in parallel.

panel_notes.topic: CCA customers keep IOU delivery demand charges
panel_notes.note: For CCA-served sites, the IOU distribution demand charges (SCE FRD, PG&E max demand, SDG&E non-coincident) remain on the bill, so demand-charge savings largely survive CCA enrollment. Generation-side TOU or demand savings depend on the CCA's own tariff, so model bundled and CCA variants separately.

With SGIP closed since 2025-12-31 and DSGS Option 3 closed to new aggregations for 2026, there is no state upfront incentive and no large VPP capacity program open to a new C&I fleet today. Underwrite on bill savings, the federal ITC and ELRP A.4 ($2/kWh). Treat DSGS 2027 and any successor (e.g., a CPUC or CEC VPP or DR redesign) as upside only.
In CAISO the durable VPP revenue is bilateral RA sold to CCAs or other LSEs through PDR registration. Slice-of-day RA counting favors 4-hour-capable aggregations, so 2-hour units are derated.

Every product here exceeds the CFC 50 kWh-per-unit indoor limit, and a single 600 kWh cabinet consumes the 600 kWh lithium-ion fire-area allowance. Indoor installs need UL 9540A data and AHJ approval. In LA and SF, plan on outdoor pads with 10 ft separation unless test data support less.

Under Rule 21 non-export (Screen I, certified UL 1741 CRD PCS), discharge must track site load at a sub-second to seconds timescale. At low-load retail sites in the evening, a 200 kW inverter may only deliver 60-100 kW. Size kW to the 4-9pm load floor, not to peak.

Grid charging of 200 kW units adds load on the service and transformer. If charging coincides with daytime peaks it can trigger Rule 15/16 upgrades, or raise the FRD/max-demand charge the battery is meant to cut. Schedule charging in the 8am-4pm super-off-peak hours with a demand-cap guard.

Permits filed on or after 2026-01-01 fall under the 2025 California Building Standards Code (CFC and CEC). Confirm the applicable edition with each AHJ, because Section 1207 and Article 706 details changed between cycles.
